## Appearance

Pembroke is a tall woman who features dark hair, dark eyes, and a remarkably determined mouth. She also has a wrinkled cheek.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Nell’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Pembroke is known to be extremely firm when dealing with her children. She is also characterized as being highly stubborn and unreasonable.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P57](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0057), [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P69](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0069)_

## History

Pembroke resided at the property known as [Pear Hill](../codex/places.md#pear-hill). After [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) slipped off a kitchen roof ridgepole and broke her ankle at a party held by his daughter Isolde, Pembroke carried the injured girl home to [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md). Later, he drove [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde to Aunt Lavinia's home in [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood) so the girls could visit the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition), and he subsequently picked them up at the end of their city trip to bring them home.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Obed Abernethy Is Surprised P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. ## Quotes

> "and I am unable to stop her, because her father encourages and helps her. A book is something she is constantly reading. Having the possibility of a playmate makes me happy—maybe she will spend more time outside because of it."
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022)

> “It’s the most delicious I’ve ever tasted,” Isolde remarked. “It is far better than the one Mrs. Sowerby makes, despite how much she boasts about her own. The flavor is completely different from hers.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P26](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0026)

> "Oh, Nell, regardless of how she got to that place, it was Aunt Lavinia. Oh, and her anger is bound to be immense, I am sure. It’s terrible—it truly is terrible—yet Nell, have you ever encountered a thing quite this amusing?"
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)

> “Is it probable that I would act in that way?” Isolde asked with righteous contempt. “Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)

> “Well, she is inside the room,” Isolde stated. “If you wish to, you may enter. I would not have the courage. Furthermore, I do not think you will accomplish anything at all.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P75](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0075)

## Relationships

### [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/isolde-pembroke--pembroke.md)

Mrs. Pembroke is the mother of [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md), who became best friends with [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) after meeting her at [Pear Hill](../codex/places.md#pear-hill). Mrs. Pembroke hosted a party where [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) suffered a broken ankle, leading Mr. Pembroke to carry the injured girl home.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Obed Abernethy Is Surprised P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P0](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0000), +17 more_

### [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/pembroke--thirza-abernethy.md)

Mrs. Pembroke and [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) are local acquaintances whose relationship turned tense after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) accidentally served Isolde three-year-old currant wine. Though Mrs. Pembroke initially rebuffed Thirza's attempts to explain the mistake and coldly turned [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) away, she later sent an apology to [Thirza](../character/thirza-abernethy.md) for the misunderstanding. By Volume 3, the two share a common anger alongside other local figures regarding children's phantom stories.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P7](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0007), [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P29](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0029), +10 more_
